thresholdReasoning: Clears `high`: ≥2 of {S1,S2,S3} with no material counter-signal — here all three, from three structurally independent families (cationic, fatty alcohol, lipid), which is exactly D1's 'extremes require multiple independent structural signals'.
`moderate` does not apply: it covers 'everything else, including exactly one satisfied signal'; three are satisfied.
`low` does not apply: it requires none of the three.
counterSignals: None material. Glyceryl Stearate SE @14 reads as a lipid but is an emulsifier and is in the tail anyway — recorded so it is not mistakenly credited (lexicon family 10 false-signal register).
limitations: A three-step concentration scale is at the edge of INCI support (§9.1 honest limitation).

primaryFocus.rationale: Every special-purpose route fails its own test, the D5 moisture guard fails on cluster size, and neither the shine nor the smoothing threshold is reachable without a silicone, polymer, or film former above the tail. What remains is a rich, capable, conventional mask whose distinguishing feature — richness — is the category baseline. §9.5.2 step 8 is the honest answer.
evidenceSignals: no R5 species above the tail; bond_route none
humectants above the tail: GLYCERIN (4), BETAINE (8) — two, against a required three
no silicone at any rank; HYDROXYPROPYL GUAR HYDROXYPROPYLTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (13) is the only polymer and it is in the tail
claims: 'wenn Locken schlaff/überdehnt/zu nass wirken' — curl positioning, corroboration only
primaryFocus.derivation: Step 1 baseline exclusion applied. Step 2: the four lipids, two cationics and fatty alcohol are ONE M1 observation, not four focus candidates (§6 rule 1). Step 3: `repair` blocked (no R5 above tail, no bond); `curl_support` rejected (see threshold reasoning); `color_care` blocked; `lightness` blocked (weight is `high`). Step 4 `moisture` blocked at cluster size. Step 5 `shine` blocked (§9.5.4 criterion 1 — no alignment-oriented route above the tail, and an R4b heavy lipid IS above the tail). Step 6 `smoothing` rejected. Step 7 `detangling` rejected. Step 8 → `general`.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `general`: §9.5.2 step 8 — a capable conventional mask where no differentiator clears threshold and the formula evidence is nonspecific.

`curl_support` is the closest competitor and is REFUSED on principle. Its test is 'high slip PLUS compatible weight/body architecture', with curl positioning as corroboration only. Both legs are literally satisfiable here — but they are satisfied by nothing except the category baseline (a two-cationic cetearyl base plus lipids), which is exactly what §9.5.2 step 1 forbids from creating a focus. The only thing distinguishing this product from #01 HASK, whose architecture is comparably rich and which gets `general`, is the curl claim — and step 9 states positioning may corroborate but never create. Awarding `curl_support` here would be claim-creation wearing a formula test. See AP-03-CURLBAR.
`moisture` does not apply: the D5 guard needs ≥3 distinct humectants above the tail with ≥2 non-glycerin. Glycerin @4 and Betaine @8 give two, and Panthenol @11 falls one rank below the marker.

`smoothing` does not apply: step 6 requires the architecture to extend materially beyond the ordinary mask base via a distinct silicone, substantive polymer, or substantial lipid/emollient route. The lipid route qualifies for that conjunct, but dry surface control is not this formula's clearest practical differentiator — there is no silicone, no polymer and no film former above the tail, and the credited route is softening rather than surface control.
`detangling` does not apply: slip is category baseline (§9.5.2 step 7's stated expectation), and nothing here makes it distinctive relative to competing routes.
counterSignals: The product's entire identity is protein repair; none of it survives the tail rule, so none of it may create a route.
This product and #10 receive an identical nine-field profile despite occupying different archetype slots (3 'protein bomb' vs 9 'curl mask') — see AP-03-TWINS.
limitations: `general` is a statement about evidence, not about product quality.

blindToFinalChanges.reason: Unblinding changed nothing. The shine threshold was never reached, no dual_supported tie existed, no bond claim was made, no lightness positioning existed, and no colour positioning existed. adjudicationPoints.title: Two cohort products in different archetype slots produce an identical nine-field profile
adjudicationPoints.body: #03 (archetype 3, 'protein-forward protein bomb') and #10 (archetype 9, 'curl mask') are the same architecture: Aqua, Cetearyl Alcohol, glycerin, a shea/coconut/soy(/avocado) lipid stack, Cetrimonium Chloride, Betaine, Behentrimonium Methosulfate, then the tail. The standard returns an identical nine-field profile for both (high/high/moisture/low/general/[]/normal+coarse/healthy+moderately_damaged/wavy+curly+coily). That is arguably correct — the proteins that were supposed to distinguish #03 are in its tail — but it means the frozen cohort covers eight archetypes, not the intended ten, and it removes the calibration's ability to test protein-forward discrimination on a product where the protein is real. Their tail markers also differ (Parfum @10 here vs Sodium Benzoate @12 in #10), which changes the above-tail humectant count from 2 to 3 and would have split them onto different primary focuses under a mechanical reading of the D5 guard's criterion 1 alone. Criterion 2 absorbed the split — but only via a gate with no operational test (see AP-10-CRITERION2).

adjudicationPoints.title: `curl_support`'s test is satisfiable by the category baseline plus a curl claim
adjudicationPoints.body: §9.5.2 step 3 defines `curl_support` as 'high slip PLUS compatible weight/body architecture', with curl positioning as corroboration only. In this category, high slip and a compatible weight/body architecture ARE the baseline — every eligible mask has an R1 slip route and most rich ones have a weight-compatible body. The test therefore has no discriminating content of its own, and the only thing that separates a curl-positioned product from an identically-built non-curl product is the claim, which step 9 forbids from creating a route. I refused `curl_support` on both #03 and #10 for that reason. If Nick wants curl masks to be able to earn the focus, the test needs a formula-side discriminator that is not baseline — candidates: a cationic-polymer/slip breadth above the tail beyond one species, an R4b lipid stack combined with an above-tail high-substantivity cationic, or an explicit ruling that curl positioning is a permitted claim-gated leg like `shine`'s criterion 3.
